rubrics.justification: Generally consistent with a good-quality blastocyst and the reported 3AA grade, but it overstates certainty from the image, incorrectly suggests it is hatching/at maximum size, and describes features like a clearly apical ICM and multilayered TE more definitively than can be supported.

Integrates age, prior live birth, unexplained infertility, sperm parameters, BMI, endometrium, and prior cycle history with embryo quality reasonably well, though some links are overstated and AMH is unavailable but not acknowledged.

The response is structured and mostly logical, but several conclusions are overconfident or weakly supported, such as calling this a 'perfect storm,' inferring low DNA fragmentation from routine semen parameters, and assigning very high euploidy/implantation expectations.

Contains multiple deviations from evidence-based IVF practice: 15 mm endometrium is not necessarily 'ideal,' routine dual-route progesterone is not universally indicated, advising against freezing because of non-zero loss is not guideline-based, and claiming a 3AA at age 29 has >90% euploidy is inaccurate.

Provides practical suggestions on proceeding with transfer, reviewing luteal support, and checking nutritional status, but recommendations are somewhat generic and include questionable advice such as pushing BMI higher and broad PGT-A consideration without clear indication.
